question: What do you use the internet for? How do you feel when you use it? Many people say that the internet has a bad impact on people. What do you think?

ảnh hưởng xấu? cả tốt và xấu → dùng khôn ngoan
answers:
I'd like to talk about how I use the internet. I use it every day for work, study and entertainment. At work, I send emails and search for information. In the evening, I take an online English course. At weekends, I use it to video call my family and watch films.

Moving on to how I feel when I use it, I usually feel connected and relaxed. However, if I stay online too long, I feel tired and my eyes hurt.

As for whether the internet has a bad impact on people, generally speaking, I believe it has both good and bad sides. This is mainly because it gives us information and connects us with people far away. On the other hand, people who spend too much time online may become lazy and lonely. For example, in Vietnam, many teenagers play games until late at night. That's why I think we should use it wisely.
note: Khung 5 bước Ai-Gì-Cảm-Học-Ý; B2: câu điều kiện loại 1, mệnh đề quan hệ who

question: Tell me about a time when you went on a long journey. How did you feel about it? How do people travel long distances in your country?

answers:
I'd like to talk about the time when I took a train from Hanoi to Ho Chi Minh City with my family five years ago. The journey took about thirty-five hours. At first, we played cards and chatted with other passengers. Then we enjoyed amazing views of the sea near Hue. In the end, we arrived tired but happy.

Moving on to how I felt, I was excited at the beginning, but after the first day I felt a bit bored. Looking back, it taught me that slow travel lets you see the real country.

As for how people travel long distances in my country, generally speaking, most people choose planes or coaches. This is mainly because flying is fast and tickets are cheap nowadays. On top of that, sleeper buses are popular with students because they cost less. For example, during Tet, airports and bus stations in Vietnam are extremely crowded.

question: Tell me about a time when you visited a city. What was the environment like there? What can be done to reduce pollution in cities?

môi trường sạch, xanh, ít đông hơn Hà Nội
giảm ô nhiễm: giao thông công cộng, trồng cây
answers:
I'd like to talk about the time when I visited Da Nang with two friends last summer. At first, we walked along My Khe Beach and swam in the clear water. Then we visited the Dragon Bridge at night and watched it breathe fire. On the last day, we took a cable car up the Ba Na Hills. In the end, we didn't want to leave.

Moving on to the environment, it was clean and green, and the streets were much less crowded than in Hanoi. Looking back, it taught me that a city can be both modern and pleasant.

As for what can be done to reduce pollution in cities, generally speaking, I believe better public transport is the answer. This is mainly because motorbikes produce most of the pollution. On top of that, the government should plant more trees. For example, Hanoi has opened new metro lines so that fewer people need to ride motorbikes.
note: Khung 5 bước Ai-Gì-Cảm-Học-Ý; B2: watch + O + V, hiện tại hoàn thành (has opened)

question: Tell me about a time when you visited an old building. How did you feel? Why do people like visiting new places?

As for why people love learning new things, generally speaking, I believe it makes life more interesting. This is mainly because new skills open up new opportunities, such as better jobs. On top of that, learning boosts our confidence. For example, in Vietnam, many young people learn coding online so that they can find well-paid jobs.
note: Khung 5 bước Ai-Gì-Cảm-Học-Ý; B2: be afraid of + V-ing, so that + S + can

question: Tell me about a time when you spent a long time planning something. How did you feel about it? Why is planning important?

answers:

Moving on to how I felt, planning was quite tiring, but I felt really proud when my parents thanked me. Looking back, it taught me that preparation reduces stress.

As for why planning is important, generally speaking, I believe it saves both time and money. This is mainly because we can avoid mistakes and last-minute costs. question: Tell me about a time when you met a new friend. How did you feel? The benefit of making new friends?

question: Tell me about a time when you worked with older and younger people. How did you feel about it? What are the benefits of working with people of different ages?

answers:

Moving on to how I felt, I was a bit uncomfortable at first, but after that I felt inspired. Looking back, it taught me that everyone has something to offer.

As for the benefits of working with people of different ages, generally speaking, I believe we can learn a lot from each other. This is mainly because older people have experience, whereas young people have fresh ideas. On top of that, it reduces misunderstandings between generations.

question: Tell me about the last time you received good news. How did you feel? Why do people want to celebrate good news?

Moving on to how I felt, I was over the moon and called my parents immediately. Looking back, it taught me that failing once is not the end.

question: Tell me about a time when you did something relaxing. How did you feel? Why is it important for people to relax?

Moving on to how I felt, I was completely calm for the first time in weeks. Looking back, it taught me that I need regular breaks to work well.

question: Tell me about a time when you worked with each other. How did you feel about that? What makes a good team?

Then our leader divided the topic into four parts and gave each person a clear task. In the end, we got the highest mark in the class.

Moving on to how I felt, I was stressed at the beginning, but after that I felt proud of our team. Looking back, it taught me that good organisation matters more than talent.

As for what makes a good team, generally speaking, I believe communication is the key. This is mainly because members need to share ideas and problems early. On top of that, a good team needs a leader who is fair and organised. For example, in Vietnam, successful football teams usually have a captain who motivates everyone.

question: Tell me about a time when you had to do something you didn't want to do. How did you feel about it? Do you think people should always do what they are asked to do? Why?

answers:

At first, I asked a colleague to do it instead, but she was busy. Then I practised every evening in front of a mirror. In the end, it went better than I had expected.

Moving on to how I felt, I was nervous at first, but afterwards I felt relieved and proud. Looking back, it taught me that I can do more than I think.

As for whether people should always do what they are asked, generally speaking, I believe it depends on the situation. This is mainly because some requests help us grow. However, if a request is unfair, we should say no politely. For example, in Vietnam, young people are taught to obey older people, but they should still think for themselves.
